content.comment_body: Hello, I have a project using [product_name] [version_no] [article_no], but now a newer version [product_name] [version_no] [article_no] is available. Could you clarify the main differences between these two versions?
Please refer to the product note: Delivery release for [product_name] [version_no].

Thanks for sharing the link. From what I understand, the main difference is support for custom web pages with an integrated web server on each [product_name] [version_no] basic device. Since I don't use this feature, there’s essentially no change for my use case. Personally, I would prefer improvements such as analog inputs with resolution higher than 10 bits or counters supporting double integers.

You were seeking the differences—the answer is in the linked note. Regardless of your use of the extended web server, if you place a new order for [product_name], you’ll receive only the [version_no] since the previous version is no longer produced. Also, the up/down counters in [product_name] are 32-bit values and limited to 999,999.

Hello, [product_name] was originally designed to replace applications using contactors, timing relays, and similar devices. As for me, the analog resolution in [product_name] is adequate. Increasing resolution could introduce more noise and lead to unstable analog readings, potentially causing EMC issues for most [product_name] users if the resolution were raised. Regards

I agree many customers find the analog resolution of [product_name] sufficient, but I have a specific project where 10-bit resolution is inadequate and it's crucial. So, I’m among the few who require higher resolution analog inputs and counters with double integer support.

If you require better resolution for analog signals, consider using a full-featured PLC instead of a logic relay; these offer analog modules with improved accuracy. It's unrealistic to expect premium features at a basic price point. Alternatively, you might look for Modbus TCP modules with higher resolution analog inputs. You can read these values in [product_name] using a Modbus client setup. However, the main limitation is integer arithmetic in [product_name], which can result in loss of resolution through rounding, depending on your calculations. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users compared [product_name] [version_no] with its predecessor, highlighting the new feature of custom web page support via an integrated web server. However, users expressed that their main needs—higher analog input resolution and larger counter ranges—remain unmet by the latest release. It was noted that [product_name] is aimed at basic automation scenarios, and may not be suitable for more advanced requirements such as increased analog accuracy or enhanced arithmetic functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect future updates to offer analog inputs with resolution greater than 10 bits and counters capable of storing larger double integer values. They hoped the new [product_name] release would address these needs.
